speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a chest skin lesion; please describe it to me—is it raised, flat, scaly, or crusted, and have any other symptoms like pain or itching developed?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your age, history of diabetes, and a growing, asymptomatic chest lesion, could you describe its specific color, borders, and any central ulceration or crusting? Also, have you noticed any changes in the color of your fingernail beds or had any recent unexplained weight loss?
